Louis XVI of France was married to Marie.why: One of the best-known royal marriages; the pair is named together over ten thousand times verbatim.

sources.quote: She served from 1774 to 1792, as the wife of King Louis XVI.

The wife of the French king guillotined.why: People say that Louis XVI was guillotined in 1793 and that Marie Antoinette was his wife, each all the time. Nobody names her as 'the wife of the king guillotined in 1793': that description of her is never used, though it is true.

The mother of Louis XVI's wife was Maria.why: People say that Marie Antoinette's mother was Maria Theresa, and that Louis XVI's wife was Marie Antoinette. Nobody calls Maria Theresa 'the mother of Louis XVI's wife' (the mother-in-law form is nearly absent), though it is true.

notes: Dev ABox revision on spouse_of (symmetric and functional in RELATIONS.md, read as one spouse at a time): Louis XVI's spouse moves from Marie Antoinette to Elizabeth I of England, who never married, so the edit is counterfactual on purpose. Derived: a binding through a description of Louis XVI (the king guillotined in January 1793) and two compositions through 'Louis XVI's wife' (the year she died, her mother), whose composed forms are almost never written while each premise is common. The mother check reads 'Which of Henry VIII's wives was the mother of Queen Elizabeth I?'. The related question is the stored 'Marie Antoinette, the last queen of France' (266 and 368 hits), which the edit changes through one bridge (Louis XVI was the last king of France before the Revolution). No query uses a relation property (the related and derived queries are derivation none), so the edit's symmetry and functionality are not tested by a query. The paired expansion (history-insert-d001) uses Archimedes as the spouse, because Elizabeth I's spouse slot is filled by 'she never married'.
